note.explanation: TCP/IP is the main suite of protocols used for internet communication. TCP provides reliable data transfer, while IP handles addressing and routing. DNS translates domain names into IP addresses, and DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses.
examples: When a device needs an IP address automatically, DHCP performs that task.
When a domain name needs to be translated into an IP address, DNS performs that task.
note.checkAnswer: TCP provides reliable data transfer; UDP provides faster, but less reliable, data transfer.
note.simple: Think of these protocols as different helpers: TCP checks that data transfers reliably, IP handles packet addresses and routes, DNS looks up IP addresses from domain names, and DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically.
note.checkQuestion: Which protocol automatically assigns IP addresses, and which protocol translates domain names to IP addresses?
note.title: Standard Protocols in TCP/IP Communications
steps: Identify the task: reliable transfer, addressing and routing, faster transfer, name translation, or automatic IP assignment.
Match the task to the protocol: TCP, IP, UDP, DNS, or DHCP, respectively.
note.answer: DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses; DNS translates domain names to IP addresses.

explain.title: TCP/IP is the internet protocol suite
explain.body: TCP/IP (Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol) is the fundamental suite of protocols for internet communication.

explain.title: TCP and IP have different jobs
explain.body: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP): Ensures reliable data transfer. Internet Protocol (IP): Handles addressing and routing of data packets.

explain.title: UDP trades reliability for speed
explain.body: User Datagram Protocol (UDP ): Provides faster, but less reliable, data transfer.

explain.title: DNS translates names
explain.body: Domain Name System (DNS): Translates domain names to IP addresses.

explain.title: DHCP assigns addresses
explain.body: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP): Automatically assigns IP addresses.

mistakes: Do not say DNS assigns IP addresses; DNS translates domain names to IP addresses.
Do not say DHCP translates domain names; DHCP automatically assigns IP addresses.
Do not reverse the reliability comparison: TCP is reliable, while UDP is less reliable.
Do not claim UDP is the more reliable protocol; the section says it is faster but less reliable.
Do not confuse IP's addressing and routing role with TCP's reliable-transfer role.
